name: Health & Medicine
summary: AI is routine in radiology and clinical note-taking, chatbots field health questions at vast scale, AI-designed drugs reach late-stage trials, and regulators loosen some rules while tightening others.

regions.name: Imaging & diagnostics
regions.summary: Radiology makes up about three quarters of FDA-authorized AI devices. A large randomized trial and a national rollout study show AI-supported breast screening finds more cancers.

landmarks.name: MASAI trial final results in The Lancet
landmarks.summary: Swedish randomized trial of about 106,000 women: AI-supported mammography had a 12% lower interval cancer rate than standard double reading, meeting non-inferiority.

landmarks.name: FDA AI device list passes 1,500
landmarks.summary: Third-party counts of the FDA list put AI-enabled device authorizations at about 1,524 through March 2026 and about 1,600 by mid-year, roughly 76% in radiology.

landmarks.name: PRAIM: AI in German breast screening
landmarks.summary: Real-world study of about 460,000 women in Germany's screening program found a 17.6% higher cancer detection rate with AI-supported reading and no rise in recalls.

regions.whyItMatters: Imaging is where medical AI has the most approvals and the strongest trial evidence, so it shows what real clinical adoption looks like.
regions.openQuestion: Does finding more cancers with AI mean fewer deaths, and do the results hold outside European double-reading programs?

regions.name: Clinical documentation & scribes
regions.summary: Ambient AI scribes that draft visit notes have spread fast across US health systems. Studies show modest time savings, and Epic's built-in scribe now competes with Microsoft and Abridge.

landmarks.name: JAMA multisite study of AI scribes
landmarks.summary: Study of 8,581 ambulatory clinicians at five health systems linked AI scribes to about 16 fewer documentation minutes per 8 patient hours, with no significant change after hours.

landmarks.name: Dragon Copilot passes 100,000 clinicians
landmarks.summary: At HIMSS 2026 Microsoft said more than 100,000 clinicians use Dragon Copilot in daily practice and opened it to partner-built apps and agents.

landmarks.name: Two thirds of Epic hospitals use ambient AI
landmarks.summary: AJMC study of 2,784 Epic hospitals found 62.6% had adopted ambient AI by June 2025; DAX Copilot, Abridge and ThinkAndor made up over 80% of implementations.

landmarks.name: Epic rolls out its own AI Charting
landmarks.summary: Epic made its native ambient scribe, built with Microsoft technology, available to customers nationwide, competing directly with third-party scribe vendors.

regions.whyItMatters: Scribes are the fastest-adopted generative AI tool in medicine and an early test of whether AI eases clinician workload in practice.
regions.openQuestion: Do scribes reduce burnout and cost, or mainly raise visit volume and billing, and how accurate are the notes?

deepDives.title: Ambient AI Tool Adoption in US Hospitals (AJMC)
deepDives.why: Peer-reviewed snapshot of which hospitals adopted ambient AI and which vendors lead.

deepDives.title: AI scribes deliver modest time savings (TechTarget)
deepDives.why: Explainer on what the evidence says about time savings and clinician experience.

regions.name: Drug development & trials
regions.summary: The first AI-discovered drug has entered Phase III, large funding rounds continue, and US and EU regulators have published shared principles for AI use across the medicines lifecycle.

landmarks.name: Insilico starts Phase III for rentosertib
landmarks.summary: Insilico dosed the first patient in a 320-patient Phase III trial in China of its AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; the drug remains investigational.

landmarks.name: Isomorphic Labs raises $2.1B
landmarks.summary: Alphabet's drug-design unit raised a $2.1B Series B led by Thrive Capital. Its first human trials, once targeted for 2025, are now expected by the end of 2026.

landmarks.name: FDA and EMA joint AI principles
landmarks.summary: The two regulators issued 10 guiding principles for good AI practice in drug development, spanning early research, clinical trials, manufacturing and safety monitoring.

regions.whyItMatters: Drug discovery is the highest-stakes test of whether AI can speed up science, and no AI-discovered drug has yet been approved.
regions.openQuestion: Will AI-designed drugs succeed in late-stage trials at a higher rate than conventionally discovered ones?

deepDives.title: Guiding principles of good AI practice in drug development
deepDives.why: The 10 joint EMA and FDA principles in full, in a short primary document.

deepDives.title: EMA AI Observatory 2025 report
deepDives.why: European regulator's yearly review of how AI is used in medicines and what is coming.

regions.name: Patient-facing assistants & mental health
regions.summary: Hundreds of millions ask chatbots health questions weekly. Products now connect to medical records, while US states restrict AI therapy and companion bots after safety concerns.

landmarks.name: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Health
landmarks.summary: A dedicated ChatGPT space that links medical records and wellness apps; OpenAI says more than 230M people ask health and wellness questions on ChatGPT each week.

landmarks.name: Illinois bans AI therapy
landmarks.summary: Illinois law bars AI from providing therapy or making therapeutic decisions without a licensed professional, with fines up to $10,000 per violation. Nevada passed a similar limit.

landmarks.name: California SB 243 on companion chatbots
landmarks.summary: First US state law regulating companion chatbots, requiring AI disclosure and protocols for suicidal ideation and self-harm, effective January 2026.

regions.whyItMatters: This is where most people actually meet medical AI, largely outside clinical oversight and medical device rules.
regions.openQuestion: Do health chatbots improve outcomes for ordinary users, and who is liable when their advice causes harm?

regions.name: Medical AI regulation & validation
regions.summary: The FDA has relaxed oversight of decision-support software and wearables while still weighing how to handle generative AI devices. The EU has delayed high-risk rules for medical devices to 2028.

landmarks.name: FDA relaxes CDS and wellness guidance
landmarks.summary: Revised final guidances, issued without prior comment, clarified when clinical decision support software is exempt and let more non-invasive wearables count as wellness products.

landmarks.name: FDA panel on generative AI mental health devices
landmarks.summary: FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee weighed evidence and monitoring standards for generative AI therapy chatbots; the FDA had not authorized any such device.

landmarks.name: EU delays AI Act rules for medical devices
landmarks.summary: The Digital Omnibus on AI, in force since July 2026, moves high-risk obligations for AI in regulated products, including medical devices, from August 2027 to August 2028.

regions.whyItMatters: Rules written for fixed software are being stretched to cover generative models, and the outcome decides what reaches patients.
regions.openQuestion: How should regulators evaluate and monitor generative AI whose outputs vary and whose models change after approval?
